notes.note: Reviewed source and real HTTP custody for direct stream, foreground/background, continuation, visual preflight, orchestration wrapper, delegation create/continue and protected steer. Existing CLI chat lost-response tests retain the original conversation and key; new SDK and CLI delegation cases compare identical request bodies on deliberate uncertain retry. The selected twelve-file batch passed 355 tests. Ignoring supplied keys failed 44 tests across nine owners; byte-exact restoration passed all 323. SDK and CLI scoped types passed. The required-key server and durable create ledger are prerequisites for enforcement; custody does not qualify older hosts, installed packages, live providers or releases.

Traced delegate create, canonical continuation and legacy continuation flag parsing through the public SDK to real HTTP. JSON transport failures retain the chosen key and known conversation, explicit retries preserve the original body, and no automatic retry was added. Help and reference describe the stable client-turn-id flag. The real CLI chat keeper already exercises both executable entrypoints after response loss. Key replacement fault failed the intended wire and retry assertions; byte-exact restoration passed the nine-owner 323-test batch. No live provider or installed CLI claim.

Reviewed the universal authenticated request-key create ledger separately from the existing portable peer-grant attempt protocol. Local callers do not need a peer; portable lookup and grant/caller checks remain closed and unchanged. A changed portable attempt cannot evade a claimed client key. Completion requires an actual provider turn receipt; the missing-receipt regression failed before repair, and the two create owners passed 62 tests after repair. Unfinished reservations stay indeterminate without replay; finite capacity refuses new claims. This is source and local scripted proof, not a live peer journey.
